# Reconstruction Book

How would this whole library be rebuilt from a bare clone, with no backup? Everything under `db/` is derived: one command, `bin/nabu rebuild`, regenerates it from the permanent folders. Everything under `canonical/` is re-fetchable, each source by the route its class below names. Everything under `local/` is the instance — rulings, grants and enrichment products — the part a reconstruction re-decides or re-earns rather than re-downloads.

This book is that recipe, in order. It is generated by `rake reconstruction:book` from the source registry, the capability registry and the tool tasks, and the test suite guards its coverage. The everyday restore paths (carrying a backup across, or a fresh `bin/nabu quickstart`) are in [restore.md](restore.md).

## 1 · Prerequisites and tools

Clone the repository and run `bundle install` (Ruby 3.3). The external tools the enrichment lanes run on install through one idempotent rake task each:

- `rake tools:embed` — Install the WHOLE semantic-search stack (venv + model + sqlite-vec); idempotent
- `rake tools:hooks` — Install the git hook pack (pre-commit + commit-msg symlinks); idempotent
- `rake tools:stanza[lang]` — Install the silver-lemma stack (venv + stanza + models); LANG defaults to la
- `rake tools:status` — Show the tool board: what is installed, where, and what isn't

The tool recipes, the human record of what those tasks do:

- [The semantic-search tools — one-command bootstrap](manual/embed-venv.md)
- [The git hook pack — one-command install](manual/git-hooks.md)
- [The silver-lemma tools — one-command bootstrap](manual/silver-lemma-venv.md)

## 2 · The sister repositories

The sister repositories are `kind: module` sources like any other: `bin/nabu sync SLUG` fetches each into `canonical/<slug>/`, and Nabu reads it back through its seam.

- `edubba-overlay` — https://github.com/arvicco/nabu-edubba, read through `Nabu::EdubbaOverlay`
- `nabu-data` — https://github.com/arvicco/nabu-data, read through `Nabu::FormLemma`, `Nabu::LanguageDossiers`
- `nabu-lects` — https://github.com/arvicco/nabu-lects, read through `Nabu::Lects`
- `nabu-places` — https://github.com/arvicco/nabu-places, read through `Nabu::Places`

## 3 · The sources, by how they come back

Every registered source falls in exactly one class: the route by which its canonical asset would come back.

### Re-crawled on the paced rail — `rail_paced`, 6 sources

Each upstream is harvested by a polite paced crawl that resumes slice by slice: a full re-crawl is months-class wall clock. `rake rail:plan` prints the lanes and `rake rail:step[SLUG]` runs one yield-guarded slice; one slice proves the recipe, the rest is calendar time.

`damos`, `korpus16`, `mdz-protestant`, `ndl-kotenseki`, `pleias-french-books`, `wellcome`.

### Re-fetched under a recorded license grant — `granted`, 15 sources

Access rides a license grant from the source, recorded in the instance config; with it in place the adapter re-fetches like any other. Obtaining a grant is a matter between the instance holder and the source, outside this public page.

`aclt`, `starling`, plus 13 not listed (grant-gated holdings that are not public).

### Re-obtained under the source's terms — `restricted`, 4 sources

The license class forbids redistribution, so there is no public mirror to fall back on: the asset must be re-obtained from the source under its terms.

`freising` (research_private), `ociana` (research_private), `seal` (research_private),
`tipitaka-lk` (research_private).

### The local shelves — 5 shelves

The shelves are the instance's own holdings, kept under `local/`: no upstream serves them, so no class above applies. They return only from a backup, or by being authored and filed anew.

`local-language`, `local-lemmas`, `local-library`, `local-notes`, `local-source`.

### The attic — what no re-fetch restores

Some canonical trees keep files their upstream has since deleted, preserved under `canonical/<slug>/.attic/` by the fetch. These are the honest irreplaceables: no re-fetch restores those bytes, and a backup is the only route back for them. On the reference instance this book was generated from, 15 sources carry an attic:

`betamasaheft-works`, `cbeta`, `dcs`, `dharma-javanese-texts`, `dharma-khmer`, `kanripo`,
`oracc`, `papyri-ddbdp`, `perseus-greek`, `perseus-latin`, `sefaria`, `suda-translations`,
`suttacentral`, `ucd`, `ud`.

## 4 · Derivation

`bin/nabu rebuild` drops every file under `db/` and regenerates it from the three permanent folders: `canonical/` (the asset), `config/` (the project definition) and `local/` (the instance). It is run deliberately, never by an automated pass, and it is hours-class on the full library. Afterward each `bin/nabu sync` keeps the indexes current incrementally for the source it touches.

## 5 · Enrichments

These are the layers `bin/nabu rebuild` deliberately does not regenerate (the cost law): each is re-acquired, re-decided or re-earned by its own command, at its own cost in time or money.

| Layer | Cost | Producer | Command | Home |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical` | acquired | sync | `nabu sync SLUG` | `canonical/<slug>/` |
| `ledger` | log | sync | `appended by every nabu sync / rebuild / health run` | `local/history.sqlite3` |
| `project_config` | ruled | curated | `hand-edited, git-tracked` | `config/` |
| `instance_config` | ruled | write_through | `nabu enable\|disable, nabu creds set, nabu model-budget, nabu health --accept-*` | `local/config/` |
| `lect_rulings` | ruled | write_through | `nabu lect assign \| withdraw \| apply-rules` | `local/config/lect_rulings.yml` |
| `mined_links` | time_heavy | enrichment | `nabu links mine SCOPE \| nabu parallels --batch SCOPE` | `local/mined-links.sqlite3` |
| `vectors` | time_heavy | enrichment | `nabu embed` | `db/vectors.sqlite3` |
| `notes_shelf` | ruled | write_through | `nabu note URN\|CODE TEXT` | `local/shelves/local-notes/` |
| `language_dossiers` | ruled | write_through | `nabu ingest --shelf language CODE \| nabu language --export-dossiers \| nabu lect dossiers` | `local/shelves/local-language/` |
| `source_dossiers` | ruled | write_through | `nabu ingest --shelf source SLUG \| nabu list --export-source-dossiers` | `local/shelves/local-source/` |
| `place_dossiers` | ruled | curated | `hand-authored essays, read at desk time` | `local/shelves/local-place/` |
| `library_shelf` | acquired | write_through | `nabu ingest FILE\|URL` | `local/shelves/local-library/` |
| `lemma_shelf` | time_heavy | enrichment | `nabu lemma-enrich LANGUAGE (projected by --index-only)` | `local/shelves/local-lemmas/` |
| `dates_shelf` | acquired | enrichment | `nabu silver-dates --import FILE` | `local/shelves/local-dates/` |
| `meter_shelf` | time_heavy | enrichment | `nabu scan-meter --run (projected by --project)` | `local/shelves/local-meter/` |

## 6 · Verification

The published census is the reference a reconstruction is measured against. As of 17 November 2026 it stands at 2,913,884 documents and 134,069,213 passages in 289 language codes, across 353 live sources of 399 registry rows (`site/_data/census.yml`, regenerated by `rake site:refresh`). Compare a rebuilt instance's `bin/nabu status` against those figures; `rake reconstruction:census` prints its per-class source counts, its attic list and its `local/` inventory. A one-command verification card is not yet part of the toolset.

Instance-specific steps (credentials, correspondence with sources) live outside the public tree.
